findings.reason: §2's node is held to 0.2 ms per slice on a rationale that does not establish the bound is reachable, so either the decision needs the cross-slice amortization argument stated (and measured) or the s2 bound needs to be recorded as a budget allocation that may return to the lead, and as written the section will spend its budget chasing a target the plan's own evidence does not distinguish from the one it rejected.
findings.text: the decision `read-bound-per-slice` argues from "the tracked read is 1.225 ms per call over 805 launches, and the warm stationary-point solve alone is 0.63–0.82 ms in 55 launches, so launch fusion cannot bring a single call to 0.2 ms", but s2 (:81, in this same change set) still states that `support_read.read`'s "cost has never been measured", so the plan asserts both that the read's cost is 1.225 ms and that it is unknown; and the stated ground does not separate the two options it puts to the lead, because the chosen option (0.2 ms per slice at batch 16) needs the same ~6x reduction as the rejected one (0.2 ms per call) unless the 55 solve launches fuse across slices — which is exactly the launch fusion the rationale says will not rescue a single call. At 1.225 ms per call, sixteen unbatched calls cost 19.6 ms, i.e. 1.225 ms per slice, six times the bound being set.

findings.reason: the decision's choice stands or falls on the argument in the finding above; a missing pointer costs a reader one search but does not itself redirect a node.
findings.text: the decision's four measurements (1.225 ms per call, 805 launches, 0.63–0.82 ms, 55 launches) appear nowhere in the plan's own text or in any cited evidence fragment; the only corroboration anywhere is the s2 review comment at :174, which records the 1.225 ms wall as taken "at the base revision" of r-20261028T215104424875-tracked-read-h200 without stating whether that read was steady-state or rebuilding, so a reader cannot check the premise of a locked decision.
